title: Low-friction A/B Experiment SDK and Orchestrator for Model Variants
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight SDK and orchestrator that lets product and platform engineers configure per-request A/B experiments and shadowing for model variants with minimal infra changes. The goal is an end-to-end flow: declare experiment (models, exposure, cohorts), schedule exposure ramps, run predefined statistical checks, surface alerts and suggested rollbacks in Console, and expose a CLI/SDK for programmatic scheduling. Emphasize low friction for engineering teams (single-line SDK enablement), reproducible experiment definitions, safe defaults (caps, burn-in, auto-stop), and tight telemetry for postmortem and billing reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Teams can create an experiment manifest (YAML/JSON) that defines two or more model variants, exposure schedule, cohort selectors, and primary/secondary metrics
SDK provides a single-call runtime hook that marks requests for experiment routing and emits deterministic experiment ids in logs/telemetry
Console shows live exposure, per-variant metrics, and a pass/fail decision from the statistical checker within 5 minutes of initial traffic
Automatic halt and recommended rollback trigger when primary metric crosses configured delta with >95% posterior probability (or configurable threshold)
Shadowing support streams a sampled fraction of live traffic to a variant without impacting the live response path
Integrations documented: traffic routing (runtime), billing attribution, rollout audit trail, and link to stored eval artifacts
spec: Core pieces: 1) Experiment manifest schema with stable fields for variants, exposures, metrics, cohorts, and controls. 2) SDK runtime: a lightweight library (Node/Python/Go) that decorates requests with experiment metadata, performs deterministic sampling, and emits telemetry events. 3) Orchestrator service: schedules exposures, enforces safety caps, computes metrics windows, and runs statistical checks. 4) Console UI: experiment creation wizard, timeline, and suggested actions. 5) CLI: create/inspect/abort experiments for infra automation. Manifest must be immutable once a cohort is live; edits create a new experiment version. Default safety policy: max 5% initial exposure, ramp factor 2x every 24h unless signal passes. Support manual overrides. Technical constraints: orchestrator must be idempotent, scale to thousands of concurrent experiments, and store time-series with 1m resolution for first 24h then 1h aggregates for 90d. Data paths must be compatible with existing cost attribution and audit logs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-3): internal alpha — product/platform engineers enable SDK in a small set of non-critical services to verify telemetry and manifest parsing. Phase 2 (week 4-8): invite-beta with 3 customer-facing teams; add Console experiment creation UI and alerting. Phase 3 (week 9-12): GA with docs, SDK examples, and prescriptive safe defaults. Each phase gated on: telemetry correctness, latency overhead <1ms p50, no regressions in billing attribution, and successful end-to-end abort/rollback tests. Post-GA: iterate to support multi-metric decisions and cohort-aware scheduling. Rollout will include a canary of the orchestrator itself (2 nodes in dedicated infra), and a feature flag to opt-in teams to the Console creation flow.
metrics: secondary: token cost per request per-variant
secondary: hallucination proxy (fuzzy match against golden set) per-variant
operational: SDK added latency, sampling rate accuracy, telemetry delivery success
business: success-conversion or downstream metric tied to caller app (optional per-experiment)
statistical_checks: Initial implementation: Bayesian A/B check using sequential testing with posterior probability thresholds. Default test compares primary metric posterior of control vs variant; requires minimum sample N (configurable) or burn-in window (default 1h). Stopping rules: success if P(variant better) > 0.975; failure if P(variant worse) > 0.95 or if credible interval crosses configured delta for harm. Correction for multiple metrics: prioritization list in manifest; fallthrough uses a weighted composite score. Provide conservative defaults and allow teams to plug custom check functions (script or lambda). All statistical decisions must attach seed and parameters to audit log for reproducibility.
api_contract: Public API endpoints/SDK methods: 1) POST /experiments - create experiment manifest (returns id). 2) GET /experiments/{id} - status and exposure. 3) PATCH /experiments/{id}/abort - manual abort. 4) POST /experiments/{id}/override - temporarily alter exposure (requires RBAC). SDK runtime: Experiment.sample(requestContext) -> {variant, assigned?:bool, experiment_id, cohort_id}. SDK emits events: experiment.evaluated, experiment.assigned, experiment.shadowed. SDK must be async-friendly and not block request completion when telemetry delivery fails (use best-effort with local buffering).
console_integration: Experiment creation wizard: upload manifest or guided form; visualize scheduled ramps; preview cohorts as example user ids. Live dashboard: streaming exposure chart, per-variant metric curves, decision indicator (PASS/FAIL/HOLD), and recommended action buttons (increase/expose/rollback). Audit trail pane: manifest version diff, operator actions, and linked PRs or runbooks. Alerting: send to Slack + paging when auto-halt triggers or when telemetry drops below 90% delivery. Role-based access: only users with 'experiment-admin' role can create/abort/override experiments. Console will surface a compact JSON for advanced edit and a YAML export for infra-as-code.
telemetry_events: experiment.metric_report (experiment_id, variant, metric_name, value, window_start, window_end)
experiment.override (experiment_id, user, field_changed, old, new, timestamp)
data_retention: Raw per-request experiment logs: 30 days. Aggregates and metric windows: 90 days. Audit trail (manifests, decisions, operator actions): 3 years. Access controls applied per customer and experiment; sensitive fields redacted by default. All telemetry must be tagged for billing attribution. Export endpoints for historical experiments must support CSV and JSON downloads for offline analysis.
rollback_rules: Automatic halt and recommended rollback if primary metric indicates degradation with configured confidence (default: posterior >95%). When auto-halt triggers, orchestrator moves experiment to HALTED state, reduces exposure to 0, emits decision event, and creates a recommended rollback artifact with: variant to restore, time window to analyze, and associated telemetry links. Manual rollback action requires 'experiment-admin' role and creates an immediate rollout to control variant. Rollback must be non-destructive to experiment history and allow resurrection for postmortem replay.
estimate_notes: 8 points: 3 for SDK surface area (Node/Python/Go minimal APIs), 3 for orchestrator core (manifest parsing, schedule, safety caps), 2 for Console + alerts MVP. Integrations and edge-cases (multi-metric support, custom checks) scoped to follow-up cycles.
open_questions: Should default statistical test be frequentist or Bayesian? We propose Bayesian for sequential stopping — confirm with research.
What is the minimum sample size policy for low-traffic services (nightly job vs request-based)?
How to tie composite business metrics from caller apps into experiment manifests securely without leaking PII?
What RBAC granularity do we expose for cross-org collaboration (team-level vs user-level)?
